newsitem.title: CHINA: China's B shares end down on cautious sentiment.
newsitem.headline: China's B shares end down on cautious sentiment.

text.p: China's B share indices closed down on Thursday with market sentiment cautious, while A shares ended mixed in slow trade, brokers said.
Shanghai's B index edged down 0.123 points, or 0.20 percent, to 61.890 points, while Shenzhen's B index shed 0.79 points, or 0.56 percent, to end at 141.65.
In Shanghai, market sentiment was hurt by the beginning of re-registration of B-share account holders to force out illegal domestic investors, brokers said.
They said the re-registration had been ordered by securities authorities and must be completed by March 15.

"Some negative factors, such as expectations of poor results for many firms and the ban on domestic investors, are worrying the market at the moment and investors are expected to liquidate their positions further in the short term," one broker said.
Huangshan Tourism was the biggest loser on profit-taking, slipping $0.020, or 4.65 percent, to $0.410 on volume of 41,000 shares.
Hua Xin Cement was the most active share on trading between institutional investors, ending unchanged at $0.230 on volume of 2.2 million shares.
Shenzhen's B-share index ended with most institutions adopting a wait-and-see attitude ahead of the corporate reporting season, brokers said.
"Few institutions are willing to engage in large-scale trading before the long Chinese Lunar New Year Holiday," a Shenzhen broker said.
Guangdong Expressway was the worst B share performer, falling HK$0.20, or 2.77 percent, to HK$7.02 on thin trade of 46,200 shares.
Southern Glass was the most active share on volume of 822,600 shares. It slipped HK$0.10 to HK$4.39.
On the A share markets, Shanghai's A index edged down 1.784 points, or 0.19 percent, to 955.175 points while Shenzhen's A shares rose 0.98 points, or 0.29 percent, to close at 342.86.
In Shanghai, cement maker Jianfeng was the biggest loser, falling 0.23 yuan, or 3.23 percent, to 6.90 yuan, on volume of 1.7 million shares.

In Shenzhen, refrigerator maker Changsha Zhongyi, which has a venture with Swedish firm Electrolux, climbed 0.35 yuan, or 5.95 percent, to 6.23 yuan on the day's heaviest trade of 19.58 million shares on speculative buying by institutions.
